assumptions.assumption: The 'muted' styling follows the existing design system's muted/secondary text color.

clarified_description: The Pixie sandbox changelog page will display the total count of all entries found in the `changelog.json` data source. This count will appear directly beneath the main page heading, styled with muted text, and will use correct singular/plural grammar (e.g., '1 entry' vs '42 entries').

constraints.detail: The count is derived from the static `data/changelog.json` file used by the site.

must: The system shall display the total count of entries from `changelog.json` on the changelog page.
WHEN the total count is 1, the system shall display the text as '{count} entry'.
WHEN the total count is not 1, the system shall display the text as '{count} entries'.
The system shall display the entry count directly below the page heading.
The system shall apply muted styling to the entry count text.
outcome: Users can see the total number of changelog entries at a glance on the changelog page.
rationale: The feature provides immediate context to the user regarding the depth of the changelog history. By placing it under the heading and using muted styling, it remains informative without competing for visual priority with the actual changelog entries.

criteria: The count is accurate to the json source
user_stories.so_that: I can immediately know how much history is documented
user_stories.want: to see a total count of changelog entries

jobs_to_be_done: Understand the scope of historical changes available on the site
users.name: Sandbox Site Visitor
pain_points: Uncertainty about how many updates have been recorded

wont: The system won't apply any time-based filters to the count.
The system won't include entries that are not present in `changelog.json`.
